lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:132:    'Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>';

Constructor pattern matches existing tests. Good.

One subtlety about the new unit test: `runZoned` captures `print` in the zone, but the compactor might emit output via `stdout.writeln` directly rather than `print`. The removed print was a `print` call, so a print-capture guard is precisely targeted at the regression. OK.

Another subtlety: `runZoned` body is async; the print zone spec applies to the zone where the body runs; awaits within remain in the zone. Yes, Dart zones propagate across async.

Now check the header_badge_pty_test changes once more for correctness concerns:

1. Content dispatch: a possible issue — the `_readsTurnChunk()` reply's tool call arguments read big files; the tool results come back and the next request contains 'checkpoint: the word-count investigation'? No — only after a fold. If the overflow happens at second request (with tool results), the guard folds and rebuilds. Rebuilt request contains the checkpoint marker → gets 'done: recovered' (2.5s delay). 

But wait — is there a scenario where the second request does NOT overflow, and the turn continues with tool results, then the model makes a third request? The mock would serve reads again... infinite loop of reads? Pre-existing scenario design: "one turn carrying all eight reads already overflows the 16384-token window at the second request". Config caps window at 16384. That logic unchanged.

2. Removed `agentTurns` — check for other references: grep.

3. `body.contains('say hi')` — the user's E1 ask. But could the FIRST turn's rebuilt request after a fold contain "say hi"? The first ask is 'count the words', so no. Good separation of markers.

4. Comment in the mock says 'say hi' replies "hi!" — previously the fallback (3rd+ requests) replied 'hi!'. Now reads is the fallback. Comment accuracy fine.

5. The 2.5s slow delay on 'done: recovered' — ensures badge window catchable. With content addressing, the post-fold continuation is always slow. Good.

Potential issue: the 'checkpoint: the word-count investigation' check happens AFTER `body.contains('<conversation>')`. The summarizer prompt includes `<conversation>`; the agent continuation request includes the folded-checkpoint marker but does it include `<conversation>`? The `<conversation>` tag is specific to the summarizer prompt format. The continuation request is a chat request — its body contains `<folded-checkpoint>checkpoint: ...</folded-checkpoint>`. No `<conversation>` tag. OK.

But wait — could the E1 ask body also contain the checkpoint marker (if E1 refolds)? Yes: first branch catches it ('say hi' → 'hi!'). Order matters and is correct: E1 always gets 'hi!' even on refold retries. But that means if E1 re-folds, the fold retry receives 'hi!' instantly without another reads round — deterministic, no starvation. Good.

One more: after E1 turn with 'hi!' reply, does the harness expect... the test then asserts no badge. Fine.

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Fixes #1469

## Root cause (from the four red-run job logs)

Two distinct faces, one per red family:

**Face B — 3 of 4 reds (83c3f293, b183b402, 76215668, all 2026-10-10, all post-#1453), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:61`** (the badge wait). Jobs 114115713413 / 114137491055 / 114167806111: `TimeoutException after 0:00:30` waiting for `\[auto-compacted( ×\d+)? · continuing\]` while the glass already showed the turn SETTLED (`>_Fa done: recovered`, status `turn 2 · 0tok`). Every one of those screens carries the leftover debug `print` from `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart:922` (landed with #1453) — `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of 'AssistantMessage' || toolResult:…` — fused INTO the fold rule and status rows (`────I^ 36 lines above fold -ePgUpe──`, `/tmp/fabadge…tx 72%`): raw bytes written to stdout mid-run land inside the live TUI's PTY frame stream, scroll the glass, and desync the cell-diff painter. The fold badge had already painted (the raw tails show zero row-24 writes after the corruption — diffs skip cells the model believes unchanged), so the badge was destroyed on the glass and never re-emitted until the settle full-repaint. The 50 ms poller (`pty_harness.dart` `pollUntil`) can never see it. The one pre-print red (e05575f2) shows the badge painting fine mid-run (`[auto-compacted ×3 · continuing]` in its raw tail) — the print is the discriminator.

lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:132:    'Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):

[greet.py#A1B2]

2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)

Delete line 3:

Add a header and trailer:

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:

+  - nested task

## PR Description

Fixes #1469

## Root cause (from the four red-run job logs)

Two distinct faces, one per red family:

**Face B — 3 of 4 reds (83c3f293, b183b402, 76215668, all 2026-10-10, all post-#1453), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:61`** (the badge wait). Jobs 114115713413 / 114137491055 / 114167806111: `TimeoutException after 0:00:30` waiting for `\[auto-compacted( ×\d+)? · continuing\]` while the glass already showed the turn SETTLED (`>_Fa done: recovered`, status `turn 2 · 0tok`). Every one of those screens carries the leftover debug `print` from `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart:922` (landed with #1453) — `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of 'AssistantMessage' || toolResult:…` — fused INTO the fold rule and status rows (`────I^ 36 lines above fold -ePgUpe──`, `/tmp/fabadge…tx 72%`): raw bytes written to stdout mid-run land inside the live TUI's PTY frame stream, scroll the glass, and desync the cell-diff painter. The fold badge had already painted (the raw tails show zero row-24 writes after the corruption — diffs skip cells the model believes unchanged), so the badge was destroyed on the glass and never re-emitted until the settle full-repaint. The 50 ms poller (`pty_harness.dart` `pollUntil`) can never see it. The one pre-print red (e05575f2) shows the badge painting fine mid-run (`[auto-compacted ×3 · continuing]` in its raw tail) — the print is the discriminator.

**Face A — 1 of 4 reds (e05575f2, 2026-10-09), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:81`** (the E1 `hi!` wait). Screen: `watchdog paused — over-window compaction in progress`, `×3` badge, `turn 3`. The E1 turn re-overflowed (its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — host estimator jitter flips it) and the request-COUNT-scripted mock handed the next reply to a fold RETRY, starving the real turn; the relief chain then outlived the 30 s budget.

## Delivered

- [x] **Product fix**: the debug `print` (+ its `// ignore: avoid_print`) removed from the structured compactor's summarize path — no more raw writes into the live PTY mid-run
- [x] **Regression guard (unit, PTY-free)**: `structured_engine_test` runs a full fold inside a zone print-capture and fails on ANY stdout output from the compaction path
- [x] **Test determinism**: the badge mock dispatches on payload (`say hi` ask / turn-1 checkpoint marker / first reads turn) instead of a request counter — every fold retry re-receives its own reply, reply slots cannot drift; `done: recovered` and `hi!` waits 30 s → 90 s (the red relief chain outlived 30 s; the 5-min test timeout still bounds the worst case). Badge waits unchanged — they are anchored sustained-window waits; the corruption vector was the print
- [x] Shared harness (`pty_harness.dart`) untouched; strictly additive vs PRs #1487/#1488/#1491

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched** — contested file (#1484/#1487/bot #1468 edit it). lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:132:    'Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,

+    extra = compute(name)

If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.

- **Branch**: `fix/1469-fold-status-row-badge-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3

- **Deletions**: -16
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T12:49:43Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T13:55:21Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1469

## Root cause (from the four red-run job logs)

Two distinct faces, one per red family:

**Face B — 3 of 4 reds (83c3f293, b183b402, 76215668, all 2026-10-10, all post-#1453), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:61`** (the badge wait). Jobs 114115713413 / 114137491055 / 114167806111: `TimeoutException after 0:00:30` waiting for `\[auto-compacted( ×\d+)? · continuing\]` while the glass already showed the turn SETTLED (`>_Fa done: recovered`, status `turn 2 · 0tok`). Every one of those screens carries the leftover debug `print` from `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart:922` (landed with #1453) — `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of 'AssistantMessage' || toolResult:…` — fused INTO the fold rule and status rows (`────I^ 36 lines above fold -ePgUpe──`, `/tmp/fabadge…tx 72%`): raw bytes written to stdout mid-run land inside the live TUI's PTY frame stream, scroll the glass, and desync the cell-diff painter. The fold badge had already painted (the raw tails show zero row-24 writes after the corruption — diffs skip cells the model believes unchanged), so the badge was destroyed on the glass and never re-emitted until the settle full-repaint. The 50 ms poller (`pty_harness.dart` `pollUntil`) can never see it. The one pre-print red (e05575f2) shows the badge painting fine mid-run (`[auto-compacted ×3 · continuing]` in its raw tail) — the print is the discriminator.

**Face A — 1 of 4 reds (e05575f2, 2026-10-09), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:81`** (the E1 `hi!` wait). Screen: `watchdog paused — over-window compaction in progress`, `×3` badge, `turn 3`. The E1 turn re-overflowed (its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — host estimator jitter flips it) and the request-COUNT-scripted mock handed the next reply to a fold RETRY, starving the real turn; the relief chain then outlived the 30 s budget.

## Delivered

- [x] **Product fix**: the debug `print` (+ its `// ignore: avoid_print`) removed from the structured compactor's summarize path — no more raw writes into the live PTY mid-run
- [x] **Regression guard (unit, PTY-free)**: `structured_engine_test` runs a full fold inside a zone print-capture and fails on ANY stdout output from the compaction path
- [x] **Test determinism**: the badge mock dispatches on payload (`say hi` ask / turn-1 checkpoint marker / first reads turn) instead of a request counter — every fold retry re-receives its own reply, reply slots cannot drift; `done: recovered` and `hi!` waits 30 s → 90 s (the red relief chain outlived 30 s; the 5-min test timeout still bounds the worst case). Badge waits unchanged — they are anchored sustained-window waits; the corruption vector was the print
- [x] Shared harness (`pty_harness.dart`) untouched; strictly additive vs PRs #1487/#1488/#1491

## Not touched / remaining

lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:132:    'Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:

+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>';

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

## PR Description

Fixes #1469

## Root cause (from the four red-run job logs)

Two distinct faces, one per red family:

**Face B — 3 of 4 reds (83c3f293, b183b402, 76215668, all 2026-10-10, all post-#1453), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:61`** (the badge wait). Jobs 114115713413 / 114137491055 / 114167806111: `TimeoutException after 0:00:30` waiting for `\[auto-compacted( ×\d+)? · continuing\]` while the glass already showed the turn SETTLED (`>_Fa done: recovered`, status `turn 2 · 0tok`). Every one of those screens carries the leftover debug `print` from `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart:922` (landed with #1453) — `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of 'AssistantMessage' || toolResult:…` — fused INTO the fold rule and status rows (`────I^ 36 lines above fold -ePgUpe──`, `/tmp/fabadge…tx 72%`): raw bytes written to stdout mid-run land inside the live TUI's PTY frame stream, scroll the glass, and desync the cell-diff painter. The fold badge had already painted (the raw tails show zero row-24 writes after the corruption — diffs skip cells the model believes unchanged), so the badge was destroyed on the glass and never re-emitted until the settle full-repaint. The 50 ms poller (`pty_harness.dart` `pollUntil`) can never see it. The one pre-print red (e05575f2) shows the badge painting fine mid-run (`[auto-compacted ×3 · continuing]` in its raw tail) — the print is the discriminator.

**Face A — 1 of 4 reds (e05575f2, 2026-10-09), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:81`** (the E1 `hi!` wait). Screen: `watchdog paused — over-window compaction in progress`, `×3` badge, `turn 3`. The E1 turn re-overflowed (its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — host estimator jitter flips it) and the request-COUNT-scripted mock handed the next reply to a fold RETRY, starving the real turn; the relief chain then outlived the 30 s budget.

## Delivered

- [x] **Product fix**: the debug `print` (+ its `// ignore: avoid_print`) removed from the structured compactor's summarize path — no more raw writes into the live PTY mid-run
- [x] **Regression guard (unit, PTY-free)**: `structured_engine_test` runs a full fold inside a zone print-capture and fails on ANY stdout output from the compaction path
- [x] **Test determinism**: the badge mock dispatches on payload (`say hi` ask / turn-1 checkpoint marker / first reads turn) instead of a request counter — every fold retry re-receives its own reply, reply slots cannot drift; `done: recovered` and `hi!` waits 30 s → 90 s (the red relief chain outlived 30 s; the 5-min test timeout still bounds the worst case). Badge waits unchanged — they are anchored sustained-window waits; the corruption vector was the print
- [x] Shared harness (`pty_harness.dart`) untouched; strictly additive vs PRs #1487/#1488/#1491

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched** — contested file (#1484/#1487/bot #1468 edit it). The issue-drafted `header_badge_pty_test.dart` entry is left to the quarantine owners; with the print gone and the mock content-addressed, the nightly repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) can un-quarantine after this lands

lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:132:    'Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.

Everything checks out. Now consider remaining findings for the exhaustive pass:

1. **BLOCKING**: none. The print removal is correct and complete (only occurrence in lib/src — verified). No CI failures input. The unit test compiles-pattern-wise; can't run dart locally (sandbox blocks it — let me try quickly anyway to see).

2. **IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION** candidates:

a) **@Timeout(5 min) vs sum of wait budgets (310s)**: waits total 60+30+90+20+90+20=310s > 300s cap. The PR claims "the 5-min test timeout still bounds the worst case" — technically the cap is now tighter than the sum of waits, so on a slow-but-progressing failure the test dies with a generic TimeoutException at 300s rather than the targeted waitFor failure. SUGGESTION: bump @Timeout to 6 min.

Wait — actually think about this more. Is it even possible for the waits to sum over 300s on the happy path? Happy path: waits resolve as soon as text appears. Worst realistic: 60+30 pass quickly, 'done: recovered' at 90 budget... if the relief chain takes 95s the waitFor times out at 90 and fails. So the elapsed time at failure ≤ 60+30+90 = 180s. The @Timeout cap is a hang-safety net. 300s vs 310s budgets: only matters if all six waits pass near their full budgets AND work time pushes over 300s — e.g., each wait passing at 95% of budget: 57+28.5+85.5+19+85.5+19 = 294.5s + fold work (folds can take real LLM-mock time — mock is instant, but PTY settle and streaming add seconds; the 2.5s slow reply etc.) — could exceed 300s while everything is actually "working". Then the test fails with a confusing generic timeout even though the badge assertions would have passed. This is plausible on a loaded runner (which is exactly the scenario the PR describes). So SUGGESTION to raise @Timeout to 6 min is legit. I'd call it SUGGESTION (test-only, failure-mode clarity) — or IMPORTANT? It affects flake behavior: a loaded runner producing near-budget waits would get a spurious generic timeout. But waits passing near budget on every step is a stretch. I'll mark SUGGESTION... hmm. Actually let me reconsider: with waits bumped to 90s the PR authors recognized the loaded-runner scenario. On a loaded runner, each wait passing at, say, 80-95% budget is realistic. Sum ~294s plus overheads (PTY spawn ~seconds, folds 2.5s each, settles 600ms×2, streaming) — 300s cap could clip a legitimate pass. That turns a would-be green into a flake — the very thing this PR fights. I'll rate IMPORTANT. Hmm, but is the timeout applied from test start including setUp? Yes, whole test body. I'll go IMPORTANT... Let me weigh: dart_test.yaml may have a global timeout preset. Check.

b) **`runZoned` print guard only catches `print`**, not `stdout.write` — but convention in lib is print; guard matches the regression vector. Not a finding (the test comment even documents intent). Could SUGGEST capturing ZoneSpecification with more... skip.

c) **Mock dispatch substring robustness**: `body.contains('say hi')` and `body.contains('checkpoint: the word-count investigation')`. Could a summarizer response/request accidentally contain 'say hi'? No. Could the reads turn request contain the checkpoint marker? No (fold hasn't happened yet). Order of branches is safe: judge → summarizer → say hi → checkpoint → reads. One scenario: E1 ask "say hi" that refolds — its rebuilt request contains both 'say hi' and checkpoint marker; first branch wins → 'hi!' quick reply. Deterministic. Good.

d) The E1-refold case means the E1 turn never gets re-reads on refold; reply is 'hi!' directly. Fine for the scenario (E1 just needs to answer hi!).

e) **`dart:async` import**: needed for runZoned/ZoneSpecification. OK.

f) Unused import check: test file already imports flutter_agent_harness etc. Fine.

g) The removed `// ignore: avoid_print` — ensure no lingering `avoid_print` ignore in engine.dart. grep.

h) One more check: `harness.waitForText('hi!')` — with content addressing, the first-turn reads replies never produce 'hi!' prematurely. Under the old counter, the third+ requests got 'hi!' — meaning mid-turn-1 a fold retry would prematurely answer 'hi!'. Fixed now. Good.

## PR Description

Fixes #1469

## Root cause (from the four red-run job logs)

Two distinct faces, one per red family:

**Face B — 3 of 4 reds (83c3f293, b183b402, 76215668, all 2026-10-10, all post-#1453), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:61`** (the badge wait). Jobs 114115713413 / 114137491055 / 114167806111: `TimeoutException after 0:00:30` waiting for `\[auto-compacted( ×\d+)? · continuing\]` while the glass already showed the turn SETTLED (`>_Fa done: recovered`, status `turn 2 · 0tok`). Every one of those screens carries the leftover debug `print` from `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart:922` (landed with #1453) — `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of 'AssistantMessage' || toolResult:…` — fused INTO the fold rule and status rows (`────I^ 36 lines above fold -ePgUpe──`, `/tmp/fabadge…tx 72%`): raw bytes written to stdout mid-run land inside the live TUI's PTY frame stream, scroll the glass, and desync the cell-diff painter. The fold badge had already painted (the raw tails show zero row-24 writes after the corruption — diffs skip cells the model believes unchanged), so the badge was destroyed on the glass and never re-emitted until the settle full-repaint. The 50 ms poller (`pty_harness.dart` `pollUntil`) can never see it. The one pre-print red (e05575f2) shows the badge painting fine mid-run (`[auto-compacted ×3 · continuing]` in its raw tail) — the print is the discriminator.

**Face A — 1 of 4 reds (e05575f2, 2026-10-09), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:81`** (the E1 `hi!` wait). Screen: `watchdog paused — over-window compaction in progress`, `×3` badge, `turn 3`. The E1 turn re-overflowed (its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — host estimator jitter flips it) and the request-COUNT-scripted mock handed the next reply to a fold RETRY, starving the real turn; the relief chain then outlived the 30 s budget.

## Delivered

- [x] **Product fix**: the debug `print` (+ its `// ignore: avoid_print`) removed from the structured compactor's summarize path — no more raw writes into the live PTY mid-run
- [x] **Regression guard (unit, PTY-free)**: `structured_engine_test` runs a full fold inside a zone print-capture and fails on ANY stdout output from the compaction path
- [x] **Test determinism**: the badge mock dispatches on payload (`say hi` ask / turn-1 checkpoint marker / first reads turn) instead of a request counter — every fold retry re-receives its own reply, reply slots cannot drift; `done: recovered` and `hi!` waits 30 s → 90 s (the red relief chain outlived 30 s; the 5-min test timeout still bounds the worst case). Badge waits unchanged — they are anchored sustained-window waits; the corruption vector was the print
- [x] Shared harness (`pty_harness.dart`) untouched; strictly additive vs PRs #1487/#1488/#1491

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched** — contested file (#1484/#1487/bot #1468 edit it). The issue-drafted `header_badge_pty_test.dart` entry is left to the quarantine owners; with the print gone and the mock content-addressed, the nightly repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) can un-quarantine after this lands
- [ ] No local execution was possible on this host: the Dart VM is SIGKILL-137 (`dart --version` → `Killed: 9`, exit 137 — same signature sibling lanes reported; openpty/PTY spawns equally sandbox-blocked) and the Dart LSP connection dies with it, so `dart analyze` and targeted tests could not run locally. ## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)

Replace line 2 with two lines:

SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"

Delete line 3:

DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:

INS.TAIL:

```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```

+  - nested task
```
</example>

No global timeout override. So the @Timeout(5 min) on the test file governs. Sum of waits = 310s > 300s. I'll flag as SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT. Given the PR itself documents the loaded-runner scenario (Face A: "an E1 re-fold on a loaded runner ground past the 30 s budget"), a loaded runner hitting near-budget waits on multiple stages is realistic; the 5-min cap could clip a legit pass and reintroduce the exact flake this PR fixes. Hmm, but consider: for the sum to approach 300s, essentially every stage must consume nearly its full wait budget — meaning the scenario itself is pathological (a healthy run completes in well under 60s total; the mock is local, replies instant except the 2.5s one). The waits pass when text appears; on a healthy run 'done: recovered' appears within ~seconds of the fold. Near-budget consumption on multiple stages simultaneously is unlikely. But "loaded runner" was precisely the observed failure mode. I'll keep it IMPORTANT — no. Let me think about the verdict impact: the machine maps any BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES; IMPORTANT/SUGGESTION → APPROVE. My verdict here: APPROVE regardless. So severity for this item is mostly informational. I'll rate it IMPORTANT (real, if edge-case, flake risk directly contradicting PR intent).

Actually, one more consideration — is it truly a risk? The @Timeout semantics: Timeout applies per test. If the test is making progress (passing waits), it just needs total ≤ 300s. For that to be exceeded with all waits passing, the run must be catastrophically slow but functional — in which case the 90s waits were the wrong fix anyway. On failure paths, the test fails fast at whichever waitFor throws. So the practical impact is: only in a "everything works but the runner is glacial" scenario does the cap clip a pass. That's a narrow window, but this file's entire history is loaded-runner flakes. IMPORTANT is fair; SUGGESTION also defensible. I'll go IMPORTANT with clear rationale.

## PR Description

Fixes #1469

## Root cause (from the four red-run job logs)

Two distinct faces, one per red family:

**Face B — 3 of 4 reds (83c3f293, b183b402, 76215668, all 2026-10-10, all post-#1453), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:61`** (the badge wait). Jobs 114115713413 / 114137491055 / 114167806111: `TimeoutException after 0:00:30` waiting for `\[auto-compacted( ×\d+)? · continuing\]` while the glass already showed the turn SETTLED (`>_Fa done: recovered`, status `turn 2 · 0tok`). Every one of those screens carries the leftover debug `print` from `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart:922` (landed with #1453) — `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of 'AssistantMessage' || toolResult:…` — fused INTO the fold rule and status rows (`────I^ 36 lines above fold -ePgUpe──`, `/tmp/fabadge…tx 72%`): raw bytes written to stdout mid-run land inside the live TUI's PTY frame stream, scroll the glass, and desync the cell-diff painter. The fold badge had already painted (the raw tails show zero row-24 writes after the corruption — diffs skip cells the model believes unchanged), so the badge was destroyed on the glass and never re-emitted until the settle full-repaint. The 50 ms poller (`pty_harness.dart` `pollUntil`) can never see it. The one pre-print red (e05575f2) shows the badge painting fine mid-run (`[auto-compacted ×3 · continuing]` in its raw tail) — the print is the discriminator.

**Face A — 1 of 4 reds (e05575f2, 2026-10-09), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:81`** (the E1 `hi!` wait). Screen: `watchdog paused — over-window compaction in progress`, `×3` badge, `turn 3`. The E1 turn re-overflowed (its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — host estimator jitter flips it) and the request-COUNT-scripted mock handed the next reply to a fold RETRY, starving the real turn; the relief chain then outlived the 30 s budget.

## Delivered

- [x] **Product fix**: the debug `print` (+ its `// ignore: avoid_print`) removed from the structured compactor's summarize path — no more raw writes into the live PTY mid-run
- [x] **Regression guard (unit, PTY-free)**: `structured_engine_test` runs a full fold inside a zone print-capture and fails on ANY stdout output from the compaction path
- [x] **Test determinism**: the badge mock dispatches on payload (`say hi` ask / turn-1 checkpoint marker / first reads turn) instead of a request counter — every fold retry re-receives its own reply, reply slots cannot drift; `done: recovered` and `hi!` waits 30 s → 90 s (the red relief chain outlived 30 s; the 5-min test timeout still bounds the worst case). Badge waits unchanged — they are anchored sustained-window waits; the corruption vector was the print
- [x] Shared harness (`pty_harness.dart`) untouched; strictly additive vs PRs #1487/#1488/#1491

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched** — contested file (#1484/#1487/bot #1468 edit it). The issue-drafted `header_badge_pty_test.dart` entry is left to the quarantine owners; with the print gone and the mock content-addressed, the nightly repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) can un-quarantine after this lands

lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:132:    'Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:

## PR Description

Fixes #1469

## Root cause (from the four red-run job logs)

Two distinct faces, one per red family:

**Face B — 3 of 4 reds (83c3f293, b183b402, 76215668, all 2026-10-10, all post-#1453), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:61`** (the badge wait). Jobs 114115713413 / 114137491055 / 114167806111: `TimeoutException after 0:00:30` waiting for `\[auto-compacted( ×\d+)? · continuing\]` while the glass already showed the turn SETTLED (`>_Fa done: recovered`, status `turn 2 · 0tok`). Every one of those screens carries the leftover debug `print` from `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart:922` (landed with #1453) — `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of 'AssistantMessage' || toolResult:…` — fused INTO the fold rule and status rows (`────I^ 36 lines above fold -ePgUpe──`, `/tmp/fabadge…tx 72%`): raw bytes written to stdout mid-run land inside the live TUI's PTY frame stream, scroll the glass, and desync the cell-diff painter. The fold badge had already painted (the raw tails show zero row-24 writes after the corruption — diffs skip cells the model believes unchanged), so the badge was destroyed on the glass and never re-emitted until the settle full-repaint. The 50 ms poller (`pty_harness.dart` `pollUntil`) can never see it. The one pre-print red (e05575f2) shows the badge painting fine mid-run (`[auto-compacted ×3 · continuing]` in its raw tail) — the print is the discriminator.

**Face A — 1 of 4 reds (e05575f2, 2026-10-09), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:81`** (the E1 `hi!` wait). Screen: `watchdog paused — over-window compaction in progress`, `×3` badge, `turn 3`. The E1 turn re-overflowed (its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — host estimator jitter flips it) and the request-COUNT-scripted mock handed the next reply to a fold RETRY, starving the real turn; the relief chain then outlived the 30 s budget.

## Delivered

- [x] **Product fix**: the debug `print` (+ its `// ignore: avoid_print`) removed from the structured compactor's summarize path — no more raw writes into the live PTY mid-run
- [x] **Regression guard (unit, PTY-free)**: `structured_engine_test` runs a full fold inside a zone print-capture and fails on ANY stdout output from the compaction path
- [x] **Test determinism**: the badge mock dispatches on payload (`say hi` ask / turn-1 checkpoint marker / first reads turn) instead of a request counter — every fold retry re-receives its own reply, reply slots cannot drift; `done: recovered` and `hi!` waits 30 s → 90 s (the red relief chain outlived 30 s; the 5-min test timeout still bounds the worst case). Badge waits unchanged — they are anchored sustained-window waits; the corruption vector was the print
- [x] Shared harness (`pty_harness.dart`) untouched; strictly additive vs PRs #1487/#1488/#1491

## Not touched / remaining

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched** — contested file (#1484/#1487/bot #1468 edit it). The issue-drafted `header_badge_pty_test.dart` entry is left to the quarantine owners; with the print gone and the mock content-addressed, the nightly repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) can un-quarantine after this lands

The fix is driven entirely from the four red-run job-log signatures (FILE:LINE above) + code reading — no local green is claimed. CI owns the verdict

lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:132:    'Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,

SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)

INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)

2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: The gh-1469 fix is sound and tightly scoped: the debug `print` in the structured compactor's summarize path is removed (verified as the only stray stdout write in `lib/src/`, consistent with the codebase's stdout-purity convention), the new zone print-capture unit test guards the exact regression vector without PTY dependencies, and the badge mock's switch from request-count to payload dispatch is deterministic — the branch ordering (judge → summarizer → `say hi` → checkpoint marker → reads) was checked and is safe for fold-retry and E1-refold scenarios.

Badge waits unchanged — they are anchored sustained-window waits; the corruption vector was the print
- [x] Shared harness (`pty_harness.dart`) untouched; strictly additive vs PRs #1487/#1488/#1491

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched** — contested file (#1484/#1487/bot #1468 edit it). The issue-drafted `header_badge_pty_test.dart` entry is left to the quarantine owners; with the print gone and the mock content-addressed, the nightly repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) can un-quarantine after this lands

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):

Add a header and trailer:

Fixes #1469

Jobs 114115713413 / 114137491055 / 114167806111: `TimeoutException after 0:00:30` waiting for `\[auto-compacted( ×\d+)? · continuing\]` while the glass already showed the turn SETTLED (`>_Fa done: recovered`, status `turn 2 · 0tok`). Every one of those screens carries the leftover debug `print` from `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart:922` (landed with #1453) — `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of 'AssistantMessage' || toolResult:…` — fused INTO the fold rule and status rows (`────I^ 36 lines above fold -ePgUpe──`, `/tmp/fabadge…tx 72%`): raw bytes written to stdout mid-run land inside the live TUI's PTY frame stream, scroll the glass, and desync the cell-diff painter. The fold badge had already painted (the raw tails show zero row-24 writes after the corruption — diffs skip cells the model believes unchanged), so the badge was destroyed on the glass and never re-emitted until the settle full-repaint. The 50 ms poller (`pty_harness.dart` `pollUntil`) can never see it. The one pre-print red (e05575f2) shows the badge painting fine mid-run (`[auto-compacted ×3 · continuing]` in its raw tail) — the print is the discriminator.

**Face A — 1 of 4 reds (e05575f2, 2026-10-09), failed at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:81`** (the E1 `hi!` wait). Screen: `watchdog paused — over-window compaction in progress`, `×3` badge, `turn 3`. The E1 turn re-overflowed (its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — host estimator jitter flips it) and the request-COUNT-scripted mock handed the next reply to a fold RETRY, starving the real turn; the relief chain then outlived the 30 s budget.

## Delivered

- [x] **Product fix**: the debug `print` (+ its `// ignore: avoid_print`) removed from the structured compactor's summarize path — no more raw writes into the live PTY mid-run
- [x] **Regression guard (unit, PTY-free)**: `structured_engine_test` runs a full fold inside a zone print-capture and fails on ANY stdout output from the compaction path
- [x] **Test determinism**: the badge mock dispatches on payload (`say hi` ask / turn-1 checkpoint marker / first reads turn) instead of a request counter — every fold retry re-receives its own reply, reply slots cannot drift; `done: recovered` and `hi!` waits 30 s → 90 s (the red relief chain outlived 30 s; the 5-min test timeout still bounds the worst case). Badge waits unchanged — they are anchored sustained-window waits; the corruption vector was the print
- [x] Shared harness (`pty_harness.dart`) untouched; strictly additive vs PRs #1487/#1488/#1491

- [ ] **Quarantine list untouched** — contested file (#1484/#1487/bot #1468 edit it). The issue-drafted `header_badge_pty_test.dart` entry is left to the quarantine owners; with the print gone and the mock content-addressed, the nightly repeat-run proof (gh-1199 AC4) can un-quarantine after this lands

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]

2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)

Replace line 2 with two lines:

Delete line 3:

DEL 3

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:

INS.TAIL:

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
